_note: Battle royale loot (ours): how many spots each kind of place gets, and where they go. What a spot holds, and at what level, is SpeedKills' own (speedkills.json loot: a gun, a hack core, or both). The legacy game's tables, its rarity weights, spot kinds, attachments, magazines, hop-ups, helmets, ammo and care-package guns, went in Milestone 526.
_density: The owner's note, 2026-09-16: 'there needs to be much less open space and more loot, like guns available'. The places now have buildings with floors and rooms to put loot IN (src/game/brpoi.ts), so a place carries a lot of spots (its tier's) and a spot holds about three items. The field keeps fewer, so the reason to go indoors is the loot: a landing that finds nothing is the complaint this fixes. A place's spot count is its tier's, and what a spot holds is SpeedKills' own (speedkills.json loot).
_tiers: `vault` is THE VAULT's, a site on one floor of the Neon tower (neonmap.json game.sites): a dozen spots rolled richer than the hot zone, so one floor of the tower is worth the climb. Every place used to roll the same table from the same number of spots, so there was no reason to choose one place over another: you landed wherever the squad did and found the same match every time. A place has a tier now. The tier says how many spots it carries and multiplies the rarity weights above, and the result is normalised, so the owner tunes rarity in one place and the tiers stay relative to it. Ours: there is no published table to copy, but the shape (a few rich places, a lot of thin ones, one hot place a match) is what every battle royale does. (Their rarity multipliers went with the legacy roll in Milestone 526: a level on the floor is speedkills.json loot's odds.)
_sites: The small places between the big ones (br.ts's sites: the Notch, Table Station, the Crossing, the Well, Highpoint, the Sump, Motor Pool, the Relay). Each is its own tier, 'site': four spots, about eleven items, leaning a little richer than a mid place, so a detour through one is worth a gun or a kit piece and a fight over it is short. They are laid after the nine places, so the Hot Zone and the places' own rolls are what they were, and never the Hot Zone: a site is 15 to 30 m across and a Hot Zone there would be a drop spot for the whole lobby. They are paid for out of the field: the loose spots on open sand went from 20 to 2, because the sites now fill the ground between the places that the field's scatter stood in for, and the floor stays inside densityTargets.
_metro: SpeedKills' metro under the centre (city.json metro, floors.ts FLOORS): `perSide` spots down each side of the tunnel, on its floor and clear of its train and stairs, rolled at `tier` (the small sites', which leans past common), last of all and on a stream of their own, so the loot above draws exactly what it drew before there was a metro (putting the tunnel's floor in the field's own spots moved every item after them: the e2e's vault caught a supply bin at its door).
_hot: The Hot Zone is SpeedKills' centre, every match (loot.ts pickHotZone): it rolls the hot tier. The radius is what the map rings where the place gives none of its own. (The legacy game drew it from the seed among its places and laid a kitted gun in it; both went, the gun in Milestone 522 and the draw in 526.)
_bots: a bot lands unarmed and searches this long before it has its gun and a shield (ours)
_pods: a care package lands inside the next ring in rounds 2 to 4, falling this long (ours: Apex's fall time is not published)
_beam: Every item stands in a thin beam of light in its rarity's colour, fading to nothing at its top, as every item on Hyper Scape's floor does (Milestone 705, docs/PHASE_29_PLAN_THE_WHOLE_NEON_CITY.md item 11, 'loot you can see'). Before it only epic and legendary items had one, and a common or rare gun or hack core past about 20 m was a few pixels on the street. height and opacity by rarity, so the eye goes to the rare ones first; radius in metres, held at its width at holdFrom metres beyond it so a far beam stays about three pixels wide at 1080p and does not thin to nothing.
_batchCap: how many of one small loot shape (a rarity's boxes, a colour's rings or beams) can be drawn at once, within drawDistance: each shape is one instanced draw call for all its copies (loot.ts Batch)
_surface: A spot for loot has to be a surface you can stand on: a box's top counts only if it is at least minSurface metres across both ways. Without it loot landed on parapets, wall tops and stair treads, where a player sees it and cannot walk to it. A place's loot is laid from 4 m out to the place's own reach (src/config/brmap.json, br.ts's radius), never less than 34 m, so West Town's clocktower and water tower, 34 m and more from its middle, get their share.
_coreDetail: SpeedKills: how near a hack core is drawn as the bought canister (paidweapons.json props hackcore, 2,382 triangles), in metres; beyond it, the box it was (12). A match lays about 477 cores and draws loot out to drawDistance, so the canister everywhere put six figures of triangles in view, which slowed the e2e's CPU drawing until a two-page check timed out (measured 2026-09-27: 477 cores, 13 supply bins, one bin within 70 m of a landing).
_halls: SpeedKills' podium halls (city.json halls, floors.ts HALL_FLOORS, Phase 24.4): `perHall` spots over each hall's floor, clear of its columns and counters, rolled at `tier` as the metro's are, last of all and on a stream of their own; the field's own spots keep off the halls' floors (loot.ts standingSpots), so the loot outside lands exactly where it did before.
_districts: SpeedKills' districts made of the packs' own demo scenes (citydistricts.json, floors.ts DISTRICT_FLOORS, Phase 25): `perDistrict` spots on each one's canyons' floor and its walkways, a metre and more from any edge, rolled at `tier` as the halls' are, last of all and on a stream of their own, so the loot everywhere else lands where it did. `walkways`: the share of them up on the walkways, drawn until each share is met (Phase 26.4): drawn at random over the plan, the narrow walkways lost to the wide canyons' floor, 0 to 4 spots of 12 up there, where the fights over the pads' landings and the fire escapes' tops are.
_landmark: `landmark`: a district's landmark, a site in neonmap.json game.sites (Milestone 661): eight spots, twice a site's, under THE VAULT's twelve, so each of the eight districts has a place worth the drop and the tower's vault stays the richest.
